aws-redshift-s3:position-deletes:v2.notes: Redshift supports reading Iceberg tables with position deletes

aws-redshift-s3:position-deletes:v3.notes: Redshift does not support Iceberg V3

aws-redshift-s3:equality-deletes:v2.notes: Redshift supports reading Iceberg tables with equality deletes

aws-redshift-s3:equality-deletes:v3.notes: Redshift does not support Iceberg V3

aws-redshift-s3:merge-on-read:v2.notes: Redshift supports merge-on-read for Iceberg tables

aws-redshift-s3:merge-on-read:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): An UPDATE on a v3 table commits delete files rather than rewriting the table, which is merge-on-read; the Iceberg snapshot summary confirms it.

links.label: Iceberg v3 features in Amazon Redshift

aws-redshift-s3:copy-on-write:v2.notes: Redshift is merge-on-read only. A DELETE commits position delete files and leaves the data files in place, and copy-on-write cannot be selected: Redshift rejects the Iceberg write.delete.mode and write.update.mode properties outright.
caveats: CREATE TABLE ... TABLE PROPERTIES ('write.delete.mode'='copy-on-write') fails with: "write.delete.mode" cannot be used in the PROPERTIES clause of "iceberg" table
Measured from the Iceberg snapshot summary: after a DELETE, total-position-deletes is 1 and total-data-files is unchanged

aws-redshift-s3:copy-on-write:v3.notes: Redshift does not support Iceberg V3

aws-redshift-s3:schema-evolution:v2.notes: Redshift supports schema evolution for Iceberg tables including add, drop, and rename columns

aws-redshift-s3:schema-evolution:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): ADD, RENAME and DROP COLUMN are all accepted on a v3 table as metadata-only changes, with existing rows still readable afterwards.

links.label: Iceberg v3 features in Amazon Redshift

aws-redshift-s3:column-default-values:v2.notes: Column default values are a V3 feature

aws-redshift-s3:column-default-values:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): A DEFAULT literal declared at CREATE is written when a DML statement omits the column; ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT backfills a pre-existing row without rewriting data files; ALTER COLUMN SET DEFAULT and DROP DEFAULT are both accepted.
caveats: v3 only: a DEFAULT on a v2 table is refused with "Columns constraints and attributes are not supported for an iceberg table"
Only literal values; nested types cannot carry defaults
CREATE TABLE AS SELECT does not inherit defaults from the source table

links.label: Iceberg v3 features in Amazon Redshift

aws-redshift-s3:table-creation:v2.notes: Redshift supports CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE for Iceberg tables in AWS Glue Data Catalog

aws-redshift-s3:table-creation:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): CREATE TABLE ... USING ICEBERG TABLE PROPERTIES ('format-version'='3') is accepted and SHOW TABLE reports the table back as format-version 3.
caveats: Omitting 'format-version' creates a v2 table, so v3 is opt-in
Downgrading a v3 table back to v2 is not supported

links.label: Iceberg v3 features in Amazon Redshift

aws-redshift-s3:hidden-partitioning:v2.notes: Redshift supports hidden partitioning for Iceberg tables

aws-redshift-s3:hidden-partitioning:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): PARTITIONED BY with day() and bucket() transforms is stored on a v3 table and queries filter on the source column with no derived column in the schema.
caveats: On S3 Tables the CREATE-time clause is silently discarded; see that mode

links.label: Iceberg v3 features in Amazon Redshift

aws-redshift-s3:partition-evolution:v2.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): ALTER TABLE ADD, REPLACE and DROP PARTITION FIELD are all accepted, and rows written under the old and new specs read back together.
caveats: The initial spec is declared with PARTITIONED BY at CREATE; see the hidden partitioning cell

links.label: Redshift adds ALTER TABLE for Iceberg tables (May 2026)

aws-redshift-s3:partition-evolution:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): ADD, REPLACE and DROP PARTITION FIELD are all accepted on a v3 table, and rows written under the old and new specs read back together.

links.label: Iceberg v3 features in Amazon Redshift

aws-redshift-s3:multi-arg-transforms:v2.notes: Multi-argument transforms are a V3 feature

aws-redshift-s3:multi-arg-transforms:v3.notes: Redshift does not support Iceberg V3

aws-redshift-s3:time-travel:v2.notes: Redshift exposes only the current state of an Iceberg table. No time-travel syntax is accepted and no snapshot metadata table is queryable, so an older snapshot cannot be read.
caveats: Five spellings were rejected, including FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF, FOR TIMESTAMP AS OF and FOR VERSION AS OF: syntax error at or near "SYSTEM_TIME"
Iceberg metadata tables such as $snapshots and $history are not exposed either

aws-redshift-s3:time-travel:v3.notes: Redshift does not support Iceberg V3

aws-redshift-s3:table-maintenance:v2.notes: Redshift supports VACUUM for Iceberg tables including compaction and snapshot expiry
caveats: Limited to VACUUM operations

aws-redshift-s3:table-maintenance:v3.notes: Redshift does not support Iceberg V3

aws-redshift-s3:branching-tagging:v2.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): Measured in both directions. No branch or tag DDL is accepted, and although a Spark-created table carrying a branch and a tag reads fine on main, none of four ref spellings resolves -- because table names go through the Glue Data Catalog, which has no notion of an Iceberg ref.

aws-redshift-s3:branching-tagging:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): Measured in both directions on a v3 table. No branch or tag DDL is accepted, and although a Spark-created table carrying a branch and a tag reads fine on main, none of four ref spellings resolves -- because table names go through the Glue Data Catalog, which has no notion of an Iceberg ref.

aws-redshift-s3:read-support:v2.notes: Full read support for Iceberg V1 and V2 tables via Redshift Spectrum, Redshift Serverless, and provisioned clusters. Supports external schemas and three-part notation with auto-mounted catalogs. Can join Iceberg tables with local Redshift tables. Supports materialized views on Iceberg tables.
caveats: Automatic query rewriting and automatic materialized views on Iceberg tables are not supported
COPY command cannot ingest from Iceberg tables; use INSERT INTO ... SELECT or CTAS
fixed(L) and uuid types not supported
Strings larger than 16384 chars are truncated

aws-redshift-s3:read-support:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): Redshift creates, writes and reads its own format-version 3 tables; a three-row round-trip through the Glue external schema returns correctly.
caveats: Before the August 2026 release this was read-only, via v3 tables another engine created

links.label: Iceberg v3 features in Amazon Redshift

aws-redshift-s3:write-insert:v2.notes: INSERT INTO supported for Iceberg tables on Redshift

aws-redshift-s3:write-insert:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): INSERT ... VALUES and INSERT ... SELECT both commit data to a v3 table.

links.label: Iceberg v3 features in Amazon Redshift

aws-redshift-s3:write-merge-update-delet.notes: MERGE, UPDATE, DELETE supported for Iceberg tables on Redshift
Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): UPDATE, DELETE and MERGE all apply to a v3 table and the resulting rows verify; v3 uses the same DML syntax as v2.

links.label: Iceberg v3 features in Amazon Redshift

aws-redshift-s3:catalog-integration:v2.notes: Integrated with AWS Glue Data Catalog

aws-redshift-s3:catalog-integration:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): Full create/write/read/drop round-trip for a v3 table through a Glue Data Catalog external schema.
caveats: Iceberg tables must be registered in the AWS Glue Data Catalog
Writes need an external schema naming an IAM role; the auto-mounted catalog cannot write

links.label: Iceberg v3 features in Amazon Redshift

aws-redshift-s3:hive-metastore:v2.notes: Redshift uses AWS Glue Catalog for Iceberg tables

aws-redshift-s3:hive-metastore:v3.notes: Redshift does not support Iceberg V3

aws-redshift-s3:aws-glue-catalog:v2.notes: Native integration with AWS Glue Data Catalog for Iceberg tables

aws-redshift-s3:aws-glue-catalog:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): The Glue Data Catalog is the catalog Redshift uses for Iceberg: a v3 table is created, written, read and dropped through it.

aws-redshift-s3:rest-catalog:v3.notes: Redshift does not support Iceberg V3

aws-redshift-s3:nessie:v3.notes: Redshift does not support Iceberg V3

aws-redshift-s3:polaris:v3.notes: Redshift does not support Iceberg V3

aws-redshift-s3:unity-catalog:v3.notes: Redshift does not support Iceberg V3

aws-redshift-s3:variant-type:v2.notes: Variant type is a V3 feature

aws-redshift-s3:variant-type:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): Absent in both directions. Redshift refuses a VARIANT column in v3 DDL ("variant is not supported for column"), and cannot read one even from a genuine v3 table built by Spark: the read fails while parsing table metadata with "Invalid column type. Got: variant".
caveats: Redshift documents variant as unsupported in v3 tables, along with the other complex types (struct, list, map)

links.label: Iceberg v3 features in Amazon Redshift

aws-redshift-s3:shredded-variant:v2.notes: Shredded variant is a V3 feature

aws-redshift-s3:shredded-variant:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): Redshift cannot read a variant column at all -- measured against a Spark-created v3 variant table -- so a shredded variant cannot be read either. Shredding is a physical layout inside a variant column, so it cannot be reached without variant support.

links.label: Iceberg v3 features in Amazon Redshift

aws-redshift-s3:geometry-type:v2.notes: Geometry types are a V3 feature

aws-redshift-s3:geometry-type:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): Redshift refuses a GEOMETRY column in v3 DDL ("geometry is not supported for column"). The read half is unmeasured rather than absent: Spark on EMR 8.0 also refuses to declare a GEOMETRY column (UNSUPPORTED_DATATYPE), so no fixture table exists for Redshift to read.
caveats: Read support genuinely untested; no engine available here can create the fixture

links.label: Iceberg v3 features in Amazon Redshift

aws-redshift-s3:nanosecond-timestamps:v2.notes: Nanosecond timestamps are a V3 feature

aws-redshift-s3:nanosecond-timestamps:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): Redshift refuses a TIMESTAMP_NS column in v3 DDL ("timestamp_ns is not supported for column"). The read half is unmeasured rather than absent: Spark on EMR 8.0 also refuses to declare TIMESTAMP_NS (UNSUPPORTED_DATATYPE), so no fixture table exists for Redshift to read.
caveats: Read support genuinely untested; no engine available here can create the fixture

links.label: Iceberg v3 features in Amazon Redshift

aws-redshift-s3:lineage:v2.notes: Lineage tracking is a V3 feature

aws-redshift-s3:lineage:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): _row_id and _last_updated_sequence_number are populated on a v3 table and are correctly excluded from SELECT *, so existing consumers see no new columns.
caveats: Must be named explicitly; they do not appear in SELECT *
On a non-v3 table both columns resolve but return NULL
After a v2 to v3 upgrade, pre-upgrade rows return NULL until the first write

links.label: Iceberg v3 features in Amazon Redshift

aws-redshift-s3:statistics:v2.notes: Redshift reads column statistics from Iceberg manifest files for scan planning and file pruning. Writes column statistics when performing DML operations on Iceberg tables.

aws-redshift-s3:statistics:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): Iceberg column metrics are written on insert to a v3 table and the planner reads them to prune scans.

links.label: Iceberg v3 features in Amazon Redshift

aws-redshift-s3:bloom-filters:v2.notes: Redshift does not support Iceberg Parquet-level bloom filters or Puffin-based bloom filter statistics.

aws-redshift-s3:bloom-filters:v3.notes: Redshift does not support Iceberg V3

aws-redshift-s3:type-promotion:v2.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): All three widenings the Iceberg spec allows (int->bigint, float->double and a decimal precision increase at the same scale) are accepted as metadata-only changes, and narrowing back is correctly refused.

links.label: Redshift adds ALTER TABLE for Iceberg tables (May 2026)

aws-redshift-s3:type-promotion:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): int->bigint and float->double are accepted on a v3 table as metadata-only widenings, and narrowing back is correctly refused.
caveats: Limited to the promotions the Iceberg spec allows

links.label: Iceberg v3 features in Amazon Redshift

aws-redshift-s3:snowflake-horizon-catalo.notes: Redshift reaches Iceberg only through the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Snowflake Horizon is consumed over Iceberg REST, and this Redshift version has no Iceberg REST client.
caveats: CREATE EXTERNAL SCHEMA ... FROM ICEBERG REST CATALOG is not recognised: it produces the same error as a deliberately meaningless catalog clause, so the clause is discarded rather than understood

aws-redshift-s3:snowflake-horizon-catalo.notes: Redshift does not support Iceberg V3 tables. This is a Redshift engine limitation.

aws-redshift-s3:deletion-vectors:v2.notes: Deletion vectors are a V3 feature; not applicable to Iceberg V2

aws-redshift-s3:deletion-vectors:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): A DELETE on a v3 table commits a Puffin deletion vector and leaves the data files in place; the .puffin file was observed in the table's S3 prefix.
caveats: v3 tables cannot write new positional delete files, only deletion vectors
Existing v2 positional deletes stay readable and are merged into deletion vectors on the next write

links.label: Iceberg v3 features in Amazon Redshift

aws-redshift-s3:unknown-type:v2.notes: Unknown type is a V3 feature, not available in format version 2

aws-redshift-s3:unknown-type:v3.notes: Redshift is an Iceberg v2 engine: creating a format-version 3 table is refused, so no V3 type can exist here.
